subject: ventures/elevator-traffic-analysis
professional: a senior vertical-transportation (lift) consultant who does CIBSE Guide D / Barney up-peak traffic analyses at feasibility stage; first checks: are P, S and H the standard closed forms, is the flight time right in all kinematic regimes, does RTT = 2H tv + (S+1) ts + 2P tp reproduce by hand, are interval and handling capacity 300PL/RTT, and would the 'passing designs' be ones a consultant would actually propose (speed vs rise, journey time)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with my own Python (scratchpad elevator-traffic-analysis/indep.py, no import of the subject): CIBSE Guide D / Barney closed forms S = N - sum(1-Ui/U)^P, H = N - sum_j (cum Uj/U)^P, flight time derived from a symmetric jerk-limited profile with bisection on peak speed, RTT = 2H tv + (S+1) ts + 2P tp, UPPINT = RTT/L, UPPHC = 300PL/RTT. (1) Example (12 x 3.6 m, 90 each, 4 x 1275 kg, 2.5 m/s): Peters ts form RTT 147.027 s, interval 36.757 s, HC 111.0, 10.28% - `node cli.mjs --example --json` gives 147.0269, 36.7567, 111.0001, 10.2778: identical to 4 s.f.+; classic Guide D form with tf(one floor) gives 146.01 s (0.7% lower), the documented Peters eq 18 departure. (2) Unequal populations [200,150,120,100,80,60,40,30], P=10: closed form S 5.3341, H 6.7223; my 200k-trip Monte Carlo 5.335/6.721; tool 5.3341/6.7223. (3) Unequal heights + express 20 m + advance opening 0.5 s + 5% losses, by hand: dH = 22.0 + 0.7223 x 3.5 = 24.528 m, hop 4.598 m > rated-speed distance 4.267 m so ts = a/j + v/a + 4.2 = 6.867 s, running 55.66, stops 43.49, transfer 20, x1.05 = 125.11 s; tool 24.528/6.8667/125.112. (4) Flight times at d = 0.2..12 m for a fast lift (2.5, 1, 1.5) and a slow one (0.5, 1, 1, v < a^2/j): all 12 equal mine to 4 d.p. (5) Design search 5 x 1275 @ 2.5: 29.41 s / 12.85% mine vs 29.4 / 12.8 tool; 7 x 1000 @ 1.0: 23.61 s / 12.24% both. Not 4: no comparison against a published worked example or commercial package (Peters PDF and marisstella.app blocked by proxy).
evidence.completeness: README/page features walked: CLI --example, --search, --simulate, --json, file input, --print-example, bad JSON and unknown option errors; page in Chromium (Playwright on node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs copy at 375 px): Example fills and calculates, design search '161 of 512 combinations meet both targets; 7 shown', simulation check '146.3 s against 147.0 s (+0.47%); 8.32 stops against 8.33', 10-row wait sweep and chart, scrollWidth 375, no console errors; floor lines with 4 fields are rejected (parseFloors). bench/grid.md regenerates byte for byte (test). Gap: the schema featureList promises journey times; sim computes meanJourney but neither page nor CLI text shows it. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `node --test engine.test.mjs page.test.mjs`: 29 pass, 0 fail, 2.6 s. Tests include flight times against numerical integration, equal-floor classic forms, Monte Carlo of S/H/RTT, and a byte-for-byte bench regeneration that pins many engine and sim paths. Seeded 10 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 9 caught (express zone counted once, losses dropped, advance opening ignored, hop -> one floor, fractional-H interpolation index, persons rounding, lobbyFree dispatch, %POP target dropped from search, dwell doubled); 1 survived (speed axis dropped from the Pareto dominance test in searchDesigns).
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (222 lines), sim.mjs, cli.mjs, index.html script, both test files, bench/grid.mjs. One engine shared by CLI, page and bench; normalise() range-checks every input with named errors; results written with textContent only; seeded RNG so outputs reproduce. Minor: blank interval/%POP target fields become Number('') = 0 on the page (index.html:206) and the summary then reports against a 0 s target; CLI '--interval' with no value gives NaN silently; optional fields default to example values via ?? without telling the user (capacity factor 80, start delay 0).
evidence.claims: Checked: (a) '-0.83% to +1.39% over 27 buildings' - bench/grid.md, regenerated by test: backed; (b) waits 0.50-0.51 of interval at 80%, 0.92-1.03 at 100%: grid.md backed; (c) EN 81-20 persons = floor(load/75): backed for the formula (the standard also caps by car area, Table 8, not mentioned); (d) flight times 'agree with numerical integration to 1e-6 s': engine.test.mjs backed and my own derivation agrees; (e) nothing uploaded / local counts only: usage.mjs and no fetch in source; (f) disclaimer and non-affiliation on page, how-it-works and README: present; (g) served llms.txt/sitemap clean (served-copy.mjs). Not backed: SoftwareApplication featureList 'simulation with waiting and journey times' - journey times not shown anywhere a user sees. Unverified: the Strakosch 55-60% figure attributed to Peters (source PDF not reachable).
evidence.fitness: Walked the architect's feasibility job on the example 12-storey office: enter floors, get RTT/interval/HC with every term shown, search designs, simulate waits. The 4-car proposal fails 30 s/12% and the search proposes 5 x 1275 @ 2.5 m/s - the answer a consultant would give. Gaps a consultant hits: the frontier also offers 7 x 1000 kg @ 1.0 m/s and 8 x 630 @ 1.6 for a 43 m rise (lobby to L12 flight 45 s at 1 m/s) because no speed-vs-rise or time-to-destination criterion is applied; up-peak only (stated) whereas modern offices are often sized on lunch traffic.
evidence.domain: Compared with CIBSE Guide D (2015) ch. 3 and Barney's up-peak formulae as restated by Peters (2000): P = CF x CC, S and H for unequal populations, jerk-limited flight in three regimes with the sqrt(vj) cap, eq 17 floor-height interpolation, express zone, 300PL/RTT and %POP all match. Departures: ts uses flight over the average hop dH/S (Peters' improvement, documented) instead of Guide D's single-floor tf(1), +0.7% on the example; design search judges designs only on interval and %POP, with no rated-speed-for-rise or average travel/time-to-destination check that Guide D design practice applies; rated persons ignore the EN 81-20 car-area cap; no ISO 8100-32 or Guide D criteria reference for the default 30 s / 12% targets.

defects.what: Design search passes and lists designs on interval and %POP alone, with no rated-speed-for-rise or time-to-destination criterion; for the 43 m example it offers 7 x 1000 kg @ 1.0 m/s and 8 x 630 kg @ 1.6 m/s as frontier designs (lobby to top flight 45 s at 1 m/s), which a lift consultant would not propose
JSON-LD featureList claims 'random-arrival up-peak simulation with waiting and journey times'; journey times (sim.meanJourney) are computed but never shown on the page or in the CLI text report
Dropping the speed axis from the Pareto dominance filter in searchDesigns leaves every test green: no test pins the frontier beyond its first row
Blank interval or %POP target fields become Number('') = 0, so the summary reports 'above your 0 s target' and the search finds nothing, instead of an error or the default
Rated persons are floor(load/75) only; EN 81-20 takes the smaller of that and the car-area table (Table 8), which the README's 'as EN 81-20 counts them' omits

verdict: A correct, well-verified up-peak RTT tool. Five outputs recomputed with my own CIBSE Guide D / Barney implementation (example RTT 147.027 s, interval 36.757 s, 10.28%; unequal-population S/H also by Monte Carlo; unequal heights + express + losses by hand 125.11 s; 12 flight times in all regimes; two design-search rows) all match to 4 s.f.; the only departure from the classic Guide D form is Peters' documented average-hop stop time (+0.7%). 29 tests pass and 9 of 10 seeded mutants are caught thanks to a byte-for-byte bench regeneration. A VT consultant would accept it as a feasibility check within its stated up-peak-only limits; the main gap is that the design search proposes slow-speed designs (1.0 m/s for a 43 m rise) because it has no speed or time-to-destination criterion, and the featureList promises journey times the page does not show.
